extraction.name: HELVIPAD
extraction.description: A real-world dataset for omnidirectional stereo depth estimation
extraction.creator: Mehdi Zayene, Jannik Endres, Albias Havolli, Charles Corbière, Salim Cherkaoui, Alexandre Kontouli, Alexandre Alahi
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected using a custom-built rig equipped with two Ricoh Theta V 360° cameras in a top-bottom setup and a synchronized LiDAR sensor. Data were collected across distinct scenes, encompassing indoor and outdoor settings in various lighting conditions on a university campus.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The LiDAR point clouds are sparse compared to high-resolution camera images, and ground-truth depth labels cover only a fraction of the total pixels.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of paired top-bottom images with corresponding depth maps, captured from a robot navigating in dynamic human environments.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The data collection process took place between December 2023 and February 2024.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: A fully automated depth completion pipeline was used to augment training data with a significantly increased label density by using depth completion.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset was preprocessed by cropping unnecessary regions (sky, ground) and downsizing from a width of 1024 pixels to 512.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Accurate depth and disparity labels were created by projecting 3D point clouds onto equirectangular images.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: The annotations were created using a custom-built rig and a central processor managing data capture and ensuring device synchronization.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The average pixel error between 200 randomly selected LiDAR points and their image positions was 1.7 pixels.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset captures human pedestrian activity, which may include sensitive human attributes such as age, gender, and socio-economic status.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset has the potential to impact society by providing a comprehensive resource for developing and benchmarking omnidirectional depth estimation models capable of navigating in human environments.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may have biases due to the scarcity of real-world datasets from omnidirectional cameras with pixel-wise depth labels, and the spherical geometry of omnidirectional images introducing significant distortions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has limitations such as the non-linear relationship between depth and disparity, making MARE particularly useful as a scale-invariant metric for assessing performance across varying depth ranges.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset can be used for training, testing, validation, and fine-tuning of omnidirectional stereo depth estimation models.
